signals.signal: local-peer. On 27/08/2026 the BNB Governing Council supplemented the payment-institution licence of Datecs Payment Technology EAD (EIK 204733952) with services under art.4 items 2, 3(b),(c) and 5 (first proposition) of the Payment Services and Payment Systems Act: cash withdrawal from a payment account and related account-servicing operations, execution of payment transactions via payment cards, execution of credit transfers including standing orders, and ISSUING of payment instruments. Datecs is a 36-year-old Bulgarian POS-terminal and printer manufacturer; its DatecsPay arm took 1st place at Visa's 'Bulgaria Pays Digitally 2.0' awards on 19/02/2026 for the highest growth rate in number of acquired merchants (and 2nd for average Visa transactions per merchant), and at the Retail Technology Show in London on 22-23/04/2026 it marketed Android smart POS, dedicated softPOS terminals (softPOS = card acceptance running as an app on an ordinary phone or tablet, no separate reader), unattended and kiosk payment integrations and 'EU acquiring services'.
signals.source_name: Bulgarian National Bank press release PR_20260827_4_BG (Governing Council decision); Datecs newsroom
signals.implies: A Bulgarian hardware maker has just become a licensed acquirer, card issuer and cash-withdrawal service provider, so it can now bid the same merchant-acquiring, unattended and kiosk work Printec pitches with Verifone and Castles terminals plus terminal management (TMS). Printec Bulgaria should defend its terminal-estate and TMS accounts by leading with multivendor terminal management and managed field service, which Datecs does not offer, rather than competing on device price, and should treat DatecsPay as the most likely displacer at mid-market merchants and at unattended/vending estates.
signals.likelihood: High - the licence is issued and DatecsPay is already winning merchants
signals.followup: Pull the refreshed BNB payment-institution register entry for Datecs Payment Technology EAD and any DatecsPay merchant/terminal disclosures; watch whether DatecsPay starts bidding bank-outsourced acquiring or unattended estates in Bulgaria and Romania (its Danubius Exim SRL agent in Bucharest is already in the BNB register).

signals.entity: MUVU Bulgaria EOOD (plus Transactis OOD, Moneso EOOD, Octis Pay OOD)
signals.signal: local-peer, NEW ENTRANTS. On 27/08/2026 the BNB Governing Council issued an electronic-money-institution licence to 'MUVU Bulgaria' EOOD. Three further Bulgarian licences were granted earlier in 2026: 'Transactis' OOD, EMI licence 14/05/2026; 'Moneso' EOOD, EMI licence 22/04/2026; and 'Octis Pay' OOD, payment-institution licence by Decision No 63 of 24/02/2026 (Sofia, Expo 2000 Office Park). 'Coriti Software' EOOD was entered in the payment-institution register on 13/05/2026. None of these are in the Printec 164-name competitor roster. The BNB payment-institution and e-money registers were both refreshed on 31/08/2026.
signals.source_name: Bulgarian National Bank press releases (Governing Council decisions) and BNB ZPUPS public registers
signals.implies: Bulgaria is licensing roughly one new e-money or payment institution per quarter after euro adoption. Each is either a buyer of terminal, TMS and transaction-monitoring infrastructure or a future rival to Printec's POS-and-acquiring line. Printec Bulgaria should work the newly licensed PI/EMI list as a named prospect pipeline for terminal supply, terminal management and INETCO transaction monitoring, and should track which of them build acquiring in-house versus buying it.
signals.likelihood: Medium - licences granted, business models not yet public
signals.followup: Identify MUVU Bulgaria EOOD's EIK, ownership and product (wallet versus acquiring) from the Bulgarian Commercial Register and the 31/08/2026 BNB e-money register; do the same for Transactis, Moneso, Octis Pay and Coriti Software.

signals.signal: regional/local-peer. On 23/07/2026 BORICA announced that it and card-platform vendor OpenWay won two international awards - 'Excellence in Digital Innovation - Europe' and 'Best Digital Transformation Program by a Vendor' - for Bulgaria's card-payments migration to the euro, confirming that the national switch and its ATM and POS acceptance run on OpenWay's Way4 platform. On 09/07/2026 BORICA hosted a business event on the PSD3/PSR package and payment-fraud prevention, marketing its Anti-Fraud and AML service package, prevention-system integration and BIN-attack protection. [STANDING - dated 25/11/2022] its 'BORICA Nova Generatsiya' client seminar set out the strategy explicitly: a modern system for managing cards, POS and ATM devices and merchants; ProCredit Bank outsourced its entire POS-terminal servicing process including customer calls to BORICA; UniCredit Bulbank deployed BORICA's software POS; Bulgarian-American Credit Bank migrated its ATM fleet and virtual POS to Way4 and cited extended monitoring as a benefit; CEO Miroslav Vichev said 'device management and logistics management are the first things a business outsources' and 'the key to the future of the acquiring business is outsourcing'; and BORICA announced a national Unified Anti-Fraud Centre (AFC) monitoring transactions across multiple networks and channels in real time for all Bulgarian financial institutions.
signals.implies: BORICA is the national processor and it is expanding into exactly Printec's adjacent lines - ATM and POS device management, software POS and real-time transaction fraud monitoring - and it is winning bank estates by offering them as outsourcing. That is direct pressure on Printec's ATM/device telemetry and monitoring, terminal management and INETCO/FICO transaction-monitoring offers at Bulgarian banks. Printec should position INETCO as a bank-owned, multivendor telemetry-and-fraud layer that sits above BORICA's processing rather than duplicating it, and should defend x-core multivendor ATM software and field-service accounts from being absorbed into a BORICA device-management bundle.
signals.likelihood: High - BORICA already runs these services for named Bulgarian banks
signals.followup: Establish the current status of BORICA's Unified Anti-Fraud Centre (live or still a programme) and identify any Bulgarian bank that moved ATM or POS estate management to BORICA in 2026.

signals.signal: local-peer. TED contract-modification notice 451922-2026, published 01/07/2026 (modification issued 30/06/2026), confirms BORICA AD (EIK 201230426) as the contractor to the Bulgarian Ministry of e-Government for 'Acceptance and servicing of card payments of monetary obligations established and collected by the Ministry of e-Government', total payable value EUR 511,291.88, original contract dated 29/05/2023, CPV 66110000 banking services. BORICA therefore holds the acquiring rail for central-government card payments and has just had it extended/modified.
signals.implies: Central-government card acceptance in Bulgaria is a BORICA incumbency that has just been rolled forward, which closes off the public-sector acquiring route for Printec's POS and terminal-management line for the extension period. The realistic Printec play is the device layer underneath rather than the acquiring contract itself: self-service and bank kiosks, unattended terminals and terminal management for e-government payment points, sold to the ministry or to municipalities rather than through the acquirer.
signals.followup: Retrieve the modification reason and new end date for Ministry of e-Government contract 451922-2026 and check whether any e-government self-service/kiosk hardware sits outside BORICA's scope.

signals.signal: local-peer/regional. On 04/08/2026 Evrotrust announced an integrated end-to-end digital onboarding and signing workflow with identity-verification vendor Shufti and signing-orchestration vendor sproof, aimed at financial institutions: Shufti performs the biometric identity check, Evrotrust acts as the regulated qualified trust service provider issuing the qualified certificate and delivering the qualified trust services behind a qualified electronic signature (QES - the legally strongest e-signature under eIDAS, equivalent to a handwritten signature EU-wide), and sproof orchestrates the signing, with all processing on EU servers. The pitch is explicitly aimed at eIDAS 2.0 and the European Digital Identity Wallet rollout required by end-2026. Evrotrust raised EUR 6.6m from 3TS Capital Partners on 04/11/2025 to deploy the EU Digital Identity Wallet in Bulgaria and expand into DACH. Its published bank case studies include International Asset Bank (onboarding new customers in minutes using electronic identification) and Investbank.
signals.implies: Evrotrust now sells a complete eKYC-plus-qualified-signature stack to Bulgarian banks, which is head-on competition for Printec's digital-onboarding/eKYC line built on Namirial. Printec should not bid Namirial on identity capture alone against a domestic qualified trust service provider that already has the local bank references; the defensible position is to bundle onboarding with AML/KYC screening (IMTF Siron, FICO) and with branch and self-service capture, and to use the end-2026 EU Digital Identity Wallet deadline as the argument that banks need an orchestration layer rather than a single QES supplier.
signals.likelihood: High - live product with named Bulgarian bank references
signals.followup: Confirm which Bulgarian banks adopt the Shufti + Evrotrust + sproof workflow, and date the International Asset Bank and Investbank deployments.

signals.signal: local-peer (systems integrator / core banking). On 18/06/2026 Sirma announced it has become a Temenos Referral Partner, identifying and introducing qualified opportunities for Temenos core-banking solutions initially in BULGARIA AND ALBANIA - two Printec footprint countries - quoting Tsvetomir Doskov, SVP BFSI at Sirma, and Edgardo Torres-Caballero, SVP Global Partnerships at Temenos, who framed it as strengthening Temenos engagement with financial institutions in CEE. Sirma's CAR service is already listed on Temenos Exchange for clients migrating to cloud/SaaS. Sirma reported 31% FY2025 revenue growth (02/04/2026), dual-listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange on 24/02/2026, and won 'Company of the Year 2026 - ICT' at the Forbes Business Awards (30/03/2026). [STANDING - dated 12/02/2025] Sirma and BORICA are already partnered on digitalising employment records.
signals.implies: A listed Bulgarian integrator now has a formal channel into Bulgarian and Albanian bank core-banking modernisation, and core-banking replacement is precisely the moment when ATM/self-service middleware, kiosk and onboarding stacks get re-tendered. Printec should map Sirma as the likely prime on Bulgarian and Albanian Temenos programmes and pre-position x-core multivendor ATM software, APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation and kiosk integration as sub-contract scope, rather than fighting Sirma for the prime slot - especially at OTP and Raiffeisen Albania where Printec already has a relationship.
signals.likelihood: Medium - referral partnership signed, no named bank programme yet
signals.followup: Watch for the first named Bulgarian or Albanian bank Temenos programme referred by Sirma, and establish whether Sirma bids ATM/self-service scope itself or sub-contracts it.

signals.signal: local-peer (CIT / cash logistics). TED contract-modification notice 342170-2026, published 19/05/2026 (modification issued 18/05/2026), names VIP SECURITY EOOD as contractor to Bulgarian Posts (Balgarski Poshti EAD) for 'Provision of property guarding services and transport of valuable consignments and postal cargo', total payable value EUR 43,985,589.75, original contract dated 24/11/2022, CPV 79713000. CIT means cash-in-transit: armoured collection, transport and processing of banknotes and coin. VIP Security is not in the Printec competitor roster; it also appears as an Evrotrust reference customer for compliance and HR e-signature workflows.
signals.implies: VIP Security holds the largest cash-logistics contract in the Bulgarian public sector and is therefore the incumbent that Printec's cash-automation story has to displace commercially: every Glory/Sesami teller cash recycler (TCR - a machine at the counter that takes in and pays out notes, recycling them so staff never handle loose cash) and every NCR intelligent-deposit or recycling ATM Printec sells reduces the CIT trips VIP Security is paid for. Printec Bulgaria should build the CIT-cost-reduction business case explicitly against published CIT contract values like this one when pitching recyclers and APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation to Bulgarian banks and to Bulgarian Posts itself.
signals.likelihood: High - contract in force and modified this cycle
signals.followup: Get the modification reason and end date for the Bulgarian Posts contract, and check whether Bulgarian Posts has any separate cash-automation or self-service equipment procurement where Printec could bid.

signals.signal: local-peer (CIT / cash logistics). TED award notice 368387-2026, published 29/05/2026, records EGIDA-SOFIA EAD as winner of the contract from Sofia's Centre for Urban Mobility EAD (Tsentar za gradska mobilnost) for collection and armoured transport of cash from ticket sales points to the central cash office at 1 Vazrazhdane Square, plus round-the-clock physical guarding of the vault room there. Value EUR 255,646, contract dated 20/05/2026, award decision 28/05/2026, and the notice records only ONE tender received. Pricing is structured as a percentage of the collected sum for transport plus a monthly fee for vault guarding. EGIDA-SOFIA is not in the Printec competitor roster.
signals.implies: Sofia's transport operator still runs a manual cash-collection-and-vault model, awarded on a single bid, which is exactly the profile that automated deposit and recycling equipment displaces. Printec should approach the Centre for Urban Mobility and comparable Bulgarian municipal transport and parking operators with self-service payment kiosks and cash-deposit/recycling automation, using the percentage-of-collected-sum CIT pricing as the cost baseline; a single-bidder CIT market also signals thin local competition, so an automation proposal faces little incumbent pushback.
signals.likelihood: Medium - requires the buyer to re-scope from CIT services to equipment
signals.followup: Obtain the contract duration for Sofia CGM award 368387-2026 so the automation pitch can be timed to its renewal, and check whether CGM has separate ticket-machine or kiosk procurements.

signals.entity: Informatsionno Obsluzhvane AD (Bulgarian state IT company) - Thales Luna HSM support
signals.signal: local-peer (systems integrator, here acting as buyer). TED contract notice 463937-2026, published 06/07/2026 (notice issued 02/07/2026), is a tender by Informatsionno Obsluzhvane AD for 'Supply, renewal and provision of manufacturer hardware and software support for Luna Network HSM equipment', CPV 50312600, estimated value EUR 106,090, tender deadline 03/08/2026, contract running 37 months to 30/09/2028, with the National Revenue Agency, the Ministry of Environment and Water and the Ministry of Labour and Social Policy named among the served bodies. Luna Network HSM is a Thales product; an HSM (hardware security module) is the tamper-resistant appliance that holds cryptographic keys and performs PIN and card cryptography, and it is one of Printec's own catalogue lines (Thales HSM/PCI). The winner had not been published as at 31/08/2026.
signals.implies: A 37-month Thales Luna HSM support contract inside the Bulgarian state IT operator, serving the tax administration and two ministries, is a Printec product sold by somebody else. Whoever wins becomes the named Thales channel competitor in Bulgarian public sector, and the incumbency will be hard to unseat before late 2028. Printec Bulgaria should identify the awardee, register as a Thales-authorised alternative for the next cycle, and in the meantime target the adjacent Informatsionno Obsluzhvane workstreams (PKI, signing, payment cryptography) where a multivendor HSM and key-management proposition can still get in.
signals.followup: Retrieve the contract award notice for TED 463937-2026 to name the winning Thales Luna HSM reseller, and add that firm to the competitor roster.

signals.entity: Bulgarian cash-collection / self-service kiosk tail (CashTerminal - Intercapital Group AD, EasyPay AD, Fast Pay HD AD)
signals.signal: local-peer (self-service / kiosk). TED contract notice 516827-2026, published 27/07/2026 (issued 24/07/2026), is a tender by Vodosnabdyavane i Kanalizatsia - Shumen OOD for 'Collection of amounts for water and sewerage services used by consumers', estimated value EUR 460,000, duration 24 months, offer deadline 24/08/2026 - the classic contract fought over by Bulgaria's cash-collection and self-service payment networks. The named tail: CashTerminal, the trademark of BSE-listed Intercapital Group AD (EIK 200867847, a BNB-licensed e-money institution since 27/07/2017), operates 24/7 unattended self-service cash-payment terminals plus a software 'cash desk' product that turns any PC into an official payment counter, and clears its payments through Paynetics; Fast Pay HD AD (EIK 202200392) and EasyPay AD (EIK 131344648) are the other licensed bill-payment networks in the BNB e-money register. None of CashTerminal/Intercapital Group or Fast Pay HD are in the Printec competitor roster.
signals.source_name: TED - Tenders Electronic Daily, notice 516827-2026; BNB e-money register (refreshed 31/08/2026)
signals.implies: Bulgaria's utility and municipal cash-collection contracts are won by unattended-terminal networks, not by banks, and those networks buy and operate exactly the kiosk hardware and cash-handling modules Printec sells into its self-service and bank-kiosk line. Rather than bidding these service contracts, Printec Bulgaria should sell the estate underneath them - kiosks, cash acceptance and recycling modules, device telemetry and managed field service - to CashTerminal/Intercapital Group, Fast Pay HD and EasyPay, who are equipment buyers rather than pure competitors, while treating their terminal footprint as the reason banks are losing branch cash traffic.
signals.likelihood: Medium - award pending on a closed tender
signals.followup: Get the award notice for TED 516827-2026 to see which collection network won VIK Shumen; pull Intercapital Group AD's BSE financial statements for terminal counts and capex, which would size the kiosk-hardware opportunity.

coverage_notes: Fresh run, no checkpoint existed. Beat: Bulgaria long-tail and NEW competitors across every Printec line, deliberately excluding the global names that have their own units. Searched in English and Bulgarian. Primary/regulator routes actually opened: BNB press-release archive by theme (Licences and all-2026 index, server-rendered .htm, desktop UA), the four BNB ZPUPS registers as direct XLSX downloads (payment-system operators, payment institutions and e-money institutions both refreshed 31/08/2026, art.2(3)/(4) providers), BORICA newsroom pages 1-3 plus the full 'BORICA Nova Generatsiya' seminar article, Datecs newsroom, Evrotrust newsroom and customer-stories index, Sirma news index and the Temenos partner release, Paynetics site, myPOS newsroom, CashTerminal and FastPay sites, Transcard site, and the TED v3 search API for Bulgaria (CPV-filtered on banking/cash/security/HSM classes plus Bulgarian-language full-text sweeps for 'bankomat', 'terminali za samoobsluzhvane', 'retsiklirashta', 'POS terminal', 'broyach na banknoti', 'sortirane na banknoti', 'kiosk', 'ATM ustroystva', 'elektronen podpis', 'HSM', 'terminalni ustroystva'), with individual notice XML pulled for each hit to name winners and values. All ten signals carry a trigger on or after 18/05/2026, so all are inside the recency window; two carry explicit [STANDING] context (the 25/11/2022 BORICA Nova Generatsiya seminar and the 12/02/2025 Sirma-BORICA partnership) which is labelled and not presented as news. Checked every player against the 164-name roster in weekly-intelligence/references/competitors.json: genuinely absent and therefore is_new are MUVU Bulgaria, Transactis, Moneso, Octis Pay, Coriti Software, VIP SECURITY EOOD, EGIDA-SOFIA EAD, Intercapital Group AD (CashTerminal), Fast Pay HD AD, Informatsionno Obsluzhvane AD and Iris Solutions AD; Datecs, BORICA, Evrotrust, Sirma, EasyPay, Paynetics, myPOS and Transcard are already on the roster but Datecs and BORICA are filed for a materially changed position. Genuine gaps: (1) app.eop.bg, the Bulgarian national CAIS EOP procurement portal, is a JavaScript single-page app and was not queried, so below-TED-threshold Bulgarian awards - which is where most small local vendor wins sit - are not covered this run; (2) commercial Bulgarian banks are private and do not publish vendor selections, so bank ATM/POS service incumbency in Bulgaria is inferred from BORICA's own 2022 client testimony rather than from 2026 contracts; (3) no per-country ATM or POS unit counts are quoted anywhere, in line with the no-invented-numbers rule; (4) the soft-POS app-store sweep was not completed because the WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) partway through, so discovery relied on direct fetching thereafter; (5) no fresh dated trigger was found for Transcard Financial Services or myPOS Bulgaria this cycle - myPOS's newsroom's most recent post is 25/03/2026 - so neither is filed as a signal.
